sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Sign-up screen imports
sections.what: Brings in the state helper, the routing and sign-in tools, the link component, and a trophy icon. The file is marked to run in the browser.
sections.why: Likely reason: the form must respond to typing and clicks.

sections.name: RegisterPage (part 1)
sections.title: Creating the account and signing in
sections.what: When the form is sent, it posts the details to the registration endpoint. On success, it signs the new user in and moves them to onboarding with the requested page carried forward. On failure, it shows the server's message, or a generic message if something unexpected happens.
sections.why: The code comment says it signs straight in so that visitors arriving from an invite link continue where they were going. The fallback message is likely there to avoid showing raw errors.
sections.watch_out: The code does not check whether the sign-in worked, so a failed sign-in still moves the user on to onboarding.

sections.name: RegisterPage (part 2)
sections.title: Name, email, password, and age fields
sections.what: Draws the form fields: full name, email, a password with a minimum of ten characters, and a checkbox confirming the user is 18 or over. Under the checkbox, a short note says the beta is for adults only and is free.
sections.why: The page says the age rule is part of the beta's safety and legal review. The minimum length is a browser hint.
sections.watch_out: The ten-character minimum is enforced only by the browser here, so the registration endpoint must enforce it too.

sections.name: RegisterPage (part 3)
sections.title: Create Account button and sign-in link
sections.what: The Create Account button stays off until the age box is ticked and while a request is running, and it shows a spinner during the request. A link under it leads to the sign-in page.
sections.why: Likely reason: the age confirmation is required before any account is created.
sections.watch_out: The spinner is cleared only after an error, so after a successful sign-up it keeps spinning until the next page appears.

summary: The sign-up form that creates an account, signs the new user in, and moves them to onboarding.
purpose: Lets a new adult create an account.
why: New users need an account before using crews and the Decision Lab. The age box is part of the beta rules.
how: Steps in order: the form shows name, email, password, and an age checkbox. The button stays off until the age box is ticked. On submit, the form sends the details to the registration endpoint. On success, it signs in with the same details and moves the user to onboarding, carrying the requested page forward. On failure, it shows the server's message or a generic error.
inputs: Name, email, password (at least 10 characters), the age checkbox, and the callbackUrl value.
outputs: A new account on the server, a signed-in session, and a move to onboarding. Or an error message.
risks: The code does not check whether the sign-in after registration worked. The ten-character minimum is checked only in the browser. The spinner is not cleared after a successful sign-up.
debug: If sign-up works but the user is not signed in, check the sign-in step and its result. If errors show only as generic messages, check the response from the registration endpoint. If the button stays off, check the age checkbox.
